context.concept_name: Gate pipeline execution on dataset-quality tests

coverage.learning_objective: Wire a fail-closed data-quality function into an existing commit-triggered pipeline.

required_facts.statement: Run data validation before model training; unexpected features, missing features or invalid feature values should prevent the affected pipeline execution from continuing.
Represent each required schema/quality check as a named result and aggregate them into an explicit pass/fail decision under the supplied gate policy.
On a failed required test, raise or return the declared failure result and do not invoke the downstream training stage.
Retain the tested input snapshot and failed check evidence so a repaired dataset can be validated against the same requirements.
Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Suppose a dataset fixture is missing a required feature. teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Resolve the deployed registry version, artifact source and originating run. Compare that run's dataset, configuration and artifact identities with the deployment and approval record. Download the exact recorded artifact generation and verify its content identity. Inspect the referenced local commit with git rev-parse and git show to confirm that the commit exists, rather than copying a revision string into the audit. In a failure fixture, a deployment linked to artifact B while approval covers A must be flagged. Preserve missing links and mismatches explicitly. The audit connects evidence that exists; it should not infer an unrecorded training source from a familiar model name.

Walk the identity chain in order, comparing deployment to registry, registry to artifact/run, run to recorded configuration and dataset, and code record to the existing commit. Each edge can fail independently, so preserve the missing or mismatched link instead of collapsing every result into a plausible name. The exact-generation download checks content against the lineage record, while local revision inspection checks whether the referenced code exists. Together they make provenance auditable from supplied records. They do not recover an absent lineage link by guesswork, even when deployment and experiment names look similar.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Matching names are not matching lineage. A missing or mismatched run/artifact link must be reported, and an unverified revision string is not evidence that the code commit exists.
